**arXiv:math/0606435v2 [math.GT] 10 Oct 2007**

*AND OTHER LINK BRAID REPRESENTATIONS*

68 pp, 38 sections.

**Abstract.** We show that 3-braid links with given (non-zero) Alexander or Jones polynomial are ﬁnitely many, and can be effectively determined. We classify among closed 3-braids strongly quasi-positive and ﬁbered ones, and show that 3-braid links have a unique incompressible Seifert surface. We also classify the positive braid words with Morton-Williams-Franks bound 3 and show that closed positive braids of braid index 3 are closed positive 3-braids. For closed braids on more strings, we study the alternating links occurring. In particular we classify those of braid index 4, and show that their Morton-Williams-Franks inequality is exact. Finally, we use the Burau representation to obtain new braid index criteria, including an efﬁcient 4-braid test.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 2 Preliminaries, basic definitions and convent; 2.1 Links and link diagrams; 2.2 Polynomial link invariants; 2.3 Semiadequacy; 2.4 Braids and braid words; 2.5 Braid representations of links; 3.1 Strongly quasi-positive links among links ; 3.2 Uniqueness of minimal genus Seifert surfac; 3.3 Fiberedness; 4.1 Alexander polynomial; 4 Polynomial invariants; 4.2 Jones polynomial; 4.3 Q polynomial; 5 Positivity of 3-braid links; 5.1 Positive braid links; 5.1.1 The Morton-Williams-Franks bound
